notes:
# 150_scan099 — reader A

The authorial number is 46. The lighter 98 at the lower left is a separate foliation hand and is retained with the margin convention. There is no written title or date. H’s statements that this is the dossier’s final page and that the dossier ends here are editorial framing, not manuscript sentences.

The page writes (109), a flag-indexed limit expression for V_{J,L}^Z for arbitrary J and L, with two nonempty conditions. The only RHS V_d^Z also serves as the upper object of a downward annotated arrow to V_d. Its square underbracket, straight tail, vertical tilde-like mark, and (h) are preserved as diagram geometry. The accompanying marginal condition concerns ordered bands, containment of X_L^*, and the top member i_n of a flag. The main line repeats the condition after replacing a canceled clairement/claire et/claire est group with donc si and adding the raised bands/order phrase. Displays (110) and (111) have hooked arrows with h above a parenthesized tilde. The page then introduces ordered bands in the chain labeled112/111, whose last digit remains uncertain, and defines V for their tuple by an intersection, a union, and a flag-indexed limit in (113). This is a report of what the page writes, not a proof verification.

## Ink-triggered rereadings

M0733 is the written equality-shaped abbreviation for même. Four nonempty signs, two in (109) and two in (113), have phi stems and are transcribed literally as phi. The113 limit has a right head. The109 lower-stroke endpoint does not securely separate into arrow arms and remains underlined-lim/directed-limit uncertain. All continuation sequences were counted as actual ink: dot followed by rule in the marginal tuple and the ordered-bands chain; in (113), dot-rule in the LHS tuple, point-rule in the intersection chain, two dots and a rule in the union condition stack and between nonempty conditions, and dot-rule in the j-index string and Drap argument. No conventional three-dot ellipsis is silently supplied.

The target subscript of (110) is heavily retraced; a rectangular final contour overlaps a J-shaped right stem and left foot, so it is left narrowly doubtful. A small separate curled mark follows the initial J in (111); both witnesses omit it, and its identity as comma or filled 0 remains uncertain. The detached stroke above e in déf is present. The main verb is posera, with final r and a; on aura is readable and has no following comma.

## Revisions and bounds

The cancelled head group remains clairement/claire et/claire est uncertain: its middle is obscured. The separate donc si above it is replacement ink. The longer phrase J,L des bandes et J prec L, et si attaches before Z contient by a continuous curved leader. In the margin, X_J* is visible but the following canceled cap/cup is not secure. In the main clause the old star also remains uncertain; the separate live X_L* has a visible forked star.

The bottom canceled block is upside down relative to the main text. A180-degree view reveals an upper union/intersection expression ending X_L*=, a second union with a raised Z/2, and a lower relation followed by Z/2=X_L*. The former upright reading and its low-star interpretation are withdrawn. Both clear X_L* groups have ordinary upper stars and lower L feet in the correct orientation. The heavily crossed opening, indices and lower relation remain explicitly tentative. An additional unfamiliar reader viewed only the existing rotated images, without witnesses or proposed text, and corroborated these shapes. The block is printed in restored reading orientation with its original orientation stated in a source comment.

The parentheses in110 and111 enclose the wave only, with h above them. The chain label’s last digit remains112/111 uncertain; its sequence is not used to force2.

There is no securely written authorial question mark or explicit verbal doubt on the page. The transcription’s uncertainty marks identify reading limits. No mathematical slip is repaired from context, and no proof or computational check was performed. A tiny contact dot by the lower left of the big union is not in the position of a disjoint-union marker and is treated as incidental pen contact, not an extra mathematical operator.

### Root check of the finite intersection and flag indexing

Conditional on (101), expansion of a finite intersection of the V_J as unions gives the tuple-indexed union in (113). If the chosen tuple contains an incomparable pair, its intersection is empty by the result on095 in the metrizability setting. Every remaining tuple sorts and deduplicates to a flag in the union of the J_a which meets every J_a. Conversely, any such flag contains a choice j_a in each J_a, and its neighborhood intersection is contained in the corresponding tuple intersection. Thus the two families have the same union; the same argument for two sets, followed by intersection with Z, gives the set-theoretic content of (109). This checks the indexing, conditional on the earlier neighborhood-union identities. It does not independently establish the categorical colimit interpretation or the homotopy-equivalence arrows in (110) and (111). No symbol in the cancelled bottom block is supplied from this argument. See CHECK_EVENTS statement150-099-finite-union-indexing.
